clause_evidence.reasoning: All 23 samples require students to interpret displayed data through various lenses: identifying specific values, comparing quantities, finding totals through summation, and computing differences. Every item demands that the student extract meaning from visual information, which is the core competency regardless of format or question complexity.

Seven samples display table visuals as the primary data format where students must locate and interpret values from row-column structures. Students perform value lookups, compute sums, identify minimum and maximum values, and calculate differences using table data exclusively.

Sixteen samples display bar chart visuals where students interpret individual bars as representations of data values. These samples require students to read bar magnitudes, compare bar lengths, identify tallest or shortest bars, compute totals by summing, and find differences between specific bars.

Seven samples display horizontal bar graphs where data is represented with bars extending leftward along an x-axis. Students interpret bar lengths to identify maximum values, compute sums, find specific values, calculate differences between categories, and make comparisons using horizontal orientation.

Nine samples display vertical bar graphs where data is represented with bars extending upward along a y-axis. Students interpret bar heights to make pairwise comparisons, find totals through summation, identify maximum and minimum values, and compute differences using vertical orientation.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sample pool demonstrates all five decomposed requirements across multiple contexts and question types. Students encounter interpreting data in both table and bar graph formats, with horizontal and vertical bar graph orientations represented throughout the 23 samples.

decomposition.reasoning: The five requirements completely and losslessly decompose the competency statement. Interpret data is the overarching skill; tables and single bar graphs specify the formats; horizontal and vertical specify the bar graph orientations required by the competency wording. No aspect of the competency is omitted or duplicated.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: All samples present cognitive demands appropriate for Grade 3 Quarter 3. Tasks require reading single values, comparing pairs, identifying extrema, computing sums with two and three digit numbers, and finding differences. Visual layouts avoid excessive complexity and use age-appropriate graph scales with increments of 5, 10, or 20.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every sample directly requires students to interpret data from a visual representation. Whether finding a specific value, comparing two values, determining maximum or minimum, calculating totals, or computing differences, each item tasks the student with extracting meaning from displayed data consistent with the competency definition.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The 23 samples span diverse question types including value identification, pairwise comparison, maximum and minimum detection, totaling, and difference computation. Data contexts vary across animals, plants, months, school subjects, grades, and flowers. Both tables and horizontal and vertical bar graphs are represented with sufficient breadth to demonstrate the competency's full scope.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Values employed are consistent with Grade 3 expectations, typically two-digit or small three-digit numbers. Graph scales use familiar intervals. No sample introduces operations, vocabulary, or visual complexity beyond Grade 3 capability. All problem structures support independent interpretation by students at this grade level.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The sample pool exhibits variation in visual format, question type, context, and learner experience setting. Horizontal and vertical bar graphs are both present; tables provide contrast. Question types range from direct value lookup to computation and comparison. Some items include thematic context while others present data directly. Experience variations include standard, hint_gated, mastery_drill, and scaffolded.
